//: The server half. CommonJS because a resource is loaded through require(), so relative imports carry the .js extension the emit will have. `types` names only the server declarations from @kingdomsconnected/types: a resource runs in the framework's isolate, not a Node program. Here that package is linked to scripting-api/ (see package.json), so a binding and the code using it land together; a release bundle depends on the published version instead. The client half is a separate program under src/client -- the two declaration sets disagree about `Player` and cannot be loaded together. No `incremental`: a .tsbuildinfo that outlives its dist/ makes tsc exit 0 and emit nothing, which left the staged resource with no scripts to load. CMake already gates this compile on the sources, so tsc's own incrementality bought nothing.
